transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13 15:00 UTC • Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Anika (Redwood CSM); Priya (Procurement), Ethan (Legal), Sara (CTO), Tom (Infra)

Summary:
Quick workshop to triage MSA redlines, confirm DPA exceptions the customer needs, align on performance SLA language (p95 latency, availability, incident credits), and agree next steps for pricing approval and pilot acceptance criteria. Short technical deep dive on KMS options and egress constraints happened mid-call.

Topics:
- MSA redline walkthrough and exceptions
- DPA data residency and subprocessor asks
- SLA: availability and incident credit model
- KMS / keying (BYOK) and audit logs
- Pilot acceptance criteria and pricing path to commit

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay everybody thanks for joining we, um, we have about 50 minutes. quick agenda, walk through the MSA redlines you sent and then the DPA asks, SLA, and we can get into some technical bits with Luis after. sound good?
[00:12] Priya (Procurement): yes that sounds right. we want to focus on exceptions that will actually block procurement, so MSA clauses and the SLA credit model mainly.
[00:20] Ethan (Legal): and clarifying subprocessor list and colon -- and how data residency is enforced. we flagged a couple of DPA items that are nonstandard for us.
[00:28] Maya: great. luis, do you want to start with KMS constraints when we get there?
[00:32] Luis (Redwood SE): yeah i'll do the tech part. i'll also show the quick diagram for VPC peering and egress patterns. we've got two main keying options: redwood-managed KMS, or BYOK via customer KMS (we support AWS KMS + GCP KMS + Azure Key Vault). note there's a slight differences in the rollout for BYOK around rotated keys and HSM-backed keys.
[00:55] Sara (CTO): quick Q, if we do BYOK can we ensure logs don't leave our control? we have to show that key material is never exported.
[01:02] Luis: yes the key material never leaves the provider HSM. we'll push usage logs to your CloudWatch / Stackdriver or to a SIEM via the logging endpoint. caveat: some metadata from request routing will be visible in Redwood control plane metrics unless you opt for private deployment.
[01:20] Tom (Infra): private deployment is probably our preference. what's the delta on cost and timeline?
[01:27] Maya: for private we generally provide a private control plane and then a customer-managed VPC, there's an onboarding fee and longer lead time. pricing delta depends on committed capacity, we can ballpark after we see usage. also note dedicated reserved pools vs private onprem are different.
[01:45] Priya: on the MSA the procurement team is hung up on section 7.2 liability caps and indemnity. we proposed an exception to the cap for wilful misconduct and IP infringement.
[01:55] Ethan: right and in the DPA we asked for deletion guarantees and a 30 day return window for data after contract termination.
[02:05] Maya: okay those are pretty common asks. liability carveouts for IP are something we can handle with legal, wilful misconduct we need to see exact language. for deletion we have standard data retention guarantees in the DPA but we can add an escrow path for high-risk datasets.
[02:20] Ethan: can you confirm retention for logs, specifically app-level logs vs raw audio transcripts? we have to be consistent with our privacy policy.
[02:28] Anika (CSM): currently Redwood retains transcripts for X days for quality monitoring but we can turn that off and provide a no-retain mode for enterprise accounts, there's an additional surcharge.
[02:40] Sara: what's the surcharge, ballpark?
[02:43] Maya: depends — usually a percent uplift on the committed capacity. we'll include a pricing appendix in the follow-up.
[02:50] Priya: SLA: we're requesting p95 latency of <200ms for the chat endpoints and 99.95% availability with a credit model that scales. typical procurement playbook wants a 3-tier credit model.
[03:05] Luis: just to clarify, <200ms p95 is pretty aggressive for models with long context windows. are you talking baby context or 2k tokens? we can target that for embeddings or short-turn inference but for long decoding maybe different.
[03:20] Sara: mostly short form interactions token counts under 512. our main user flows are inline suggestions.
[03:26] Luis: okay that's achievable on dedicated pools. on hosted tiers we have variable tail latencies due to multi-tenant batching. dedicated or private gives you guaranteed throughput and lower p95.
[03:40] Priya: procurement likely will require SLA mapped to environment — e.g., pilot (hosted), production (dedicated).
[03:47] Ethan: also want clear incident response times and a runbook for high-severity incidents.
[03:52] Maya: we can propose SLOs: P1 ack within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 2 hours, RCA within 72 hours. credits tied to monthly uptime and p95 breaches.
[04:05] Priya: can you show an example credit formula? we usually look for a sliding scale not all-or-nothing.
[04:12] Maya: yeah for example 99.95-100% -> 0% credits, 99.5-99.95 -> 5% credits, 99.0-99.5 -> 10%, <99.0 -> 20%. for p95 breaches we'd tie token-level credits or per-hour credits.
[04:30] Ethan: that sounds reasonable. we'll still want to have a cap on cumulative credits.
[04:35] Maya: agreed. we'll propose a cumulative cap and also exclude scheduled maintenance windows.
[04:42] Tom: about egress fees — we have restrictions in our budget on outbound traffic. what are typical egress numbers for a 1M monthly token use case?
[04:52] Luis: egress is mostly dependent on payload size. with streaming, payload to customers is minimal. but embeddings and large responses can add up. typical numbers we see are X to Y TBs for that token count, we'll send a worksheet.
[05:08] Priya: please include estimated egress cost assumptions in the follow-up. procurement needs line items.
[05:12] Maya: will do.
[05:18] Ethan: one DPA point — subprocessors list. the redlines asked for a fixed list and 30-day notice for adding new subprocessors. we prefer a 60-day notice.
[05:27] Maya: internally we do 30-day notice with opt-out rights for critical subprocessors, or advance written consent depending on the risk profile. i can put both options in the annotated MSA.
[05:38] Ethan: okay we'll review.
[05:41] [05:41] Luis (Redwood SE): can i share a quick diagram? the diagram shows options: A) Hosted API (fast onboarding), B) Dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity), C) Private deployment (VPC peering/onprem). If you choose C we can disable control-plane telemetry flows, and push logs only to your SIEM. the BYOK flow ties to your KMS via a secure peering and the keys are used at inference nodes. caveat: certain quantization paths may require operator-level logs for debugging.
[06:12] Sara: that last bit — operator logs — can those be pseudonymized? we can't show customer PII.
[06:18] Luis: yes masking/pseudonymization is possible, and we support redaction rules in the ingest pipeline.
[06:24] Priya: what about SOC2 and encryption-at-rest? procurement needs docs.
[06:29] Anika: we'll share our SOC2 Type II and encryption-at-rest coverage. note that for private deployments some onprem controls change the scope.
[06:40] Tom: about the pilot acceptance criteria — we need a clear pass/fail: availability >99.9 during pilot, latency p95 less than 300ms, and no data leakage incidents.
[06:50] Maya: that seems like a fair pilot bar. suggest we define pilot duration (2 weeks at production-like traffic) and define test prompts and telemetry to validate.
[06:58] Ethan: pricing approval — we'll need a budget number and expected committed term to get internal signoff.
[07:04] Maya: usually procurement asks for three options: pilot (time-limited), 12-month commit, 36-month commit with discounts. we'll provide a price ladder.
[07:12] Priya: and can you include a binding quickstart SLA for the pilot with a lower credit cap? procurement prefers that.
[07:18] Maya: yes we'll add a pilot SLA appendix.
[07:22] [07:22] Interruption / crosstalk, faint: sound of paper shuffling
[07:30] Luis: small technical note: KV cache sizing can impact latency; if your workload has many small repetitive prefixes we recommend prefix-key caching to reduce token generation times. it's a config option but requires some instrumentation.
[07:46] Sara: good to know. we'll have a sample dataset for the pilot.
[07:51] Priya: timeline check — procurement decision target is end of November; do you think that's doable?
[07:58] Maya: yes if we get redlines back this week and run a quick legal review and a 2-week pilot mid-November, the timeline is tight but feasible.
[08:08] Ethan: on legal we need to see the annotated MSA with counter-proposals inline. can you do that by Tuesday?
[08:14] Maya: yes i'll have an annotated version Monday or Tuesday.
[08:18] Ethan: and add the DPA changes as tracked too.
[08:21] Maya: absolutely.
[08:23] [08:23] Luis: on the BYOK runbook i'll note brief steps: customer creates key in KMS, share key ARN with Redwood, Redwood creates key access role, test encrypt/decrypt handshake, rotate keys per schedule. also include key revocation and fallback so you don't lose access if keys are rotated.
[08:42] Tom: for disaster recovery, can you guarantee cross-region failover without data leaving region? we have strict residency controls.
[08:50] Luis: cross-region failover is possible but then data replication rules need to be explicit; for strict residency we'd keep primary and DR in approved regions and document the replication flows. we'll surface that in the runbook.
[09:05] Priya: a few redlines were administrative but one big ask was: unlimited audit rights for certain datasets. procurement asks for audit rights but legal is hesitant.
[09:15] Ethan: yes unlimited audit rights are ok at a high level but the scope and frequency need to be reasonable. we proposed quarterly with notice.
[09:22] Maya: we can offer a quarterly on-site / remote audit with pre-agreed scope. add cost for SOW if large.
[09:30] Sara: about the competitor note — we trialed CloudText earlier and they had inconsistent latency under load; we want a vendor that can handle bursty traffic.
[09:40] Maya: good to know. dedicated pools and autoscaling with reserved burst are exactly what we'd recommend for bursty workloads to keep tail latencies low.
[09:50] [09:50] Anika: quick administrative point — i'll put all links in the shared drive: SOC2, security questionnaire, pricing worksheet, pilot playbook, and the annotated MSA.
[09:58] Priya: excellent.
[10:00] Ethan: one more DPA ask — notifications for law enforcement requests. we need a clause on notice unless prohibited.
[10:07] Maya: standard language is we notify unless prohibited; we'll include proposed language.
[10:12] Priya: okay next steps recap, please.
[10:15] Maya: recap: i'll send annotated MSA + DPA redlines by 2025-11-18, include suggested SLA credit formula and pilot appendix; Luis will draft KMS runbook and VPC peering diagram by 2025-11-17; Anika will upload SOC2 and pricing worksheet today; customer to confirm procurement approver list and residency regions by 2025-11-20; schedule legal-only sync 2025-11-19.
[10:40] Priya: sounds good.
[10:42] Ethan: thanks everyone.
[10:44] Sara: thanks.
[10:45] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
[10:50] Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains intermittent mis-hears (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "Redword" occasionally). speaker labels from auto-transcript were corrected minimally.
